extracted.intended_audience: SEC reporting professionals / corporate accountants preparing significance tests for business combinations (registrants, auditors, in-house counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on performing the SEC 'tests of significance' (investment, income, asset tests) for business acquisitions, including what is included in the purchase price, how to compute the denominator (AWMV), step acquisitions, common-control combinations, and treatment of contingent consideration, transaction costs, and other related payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of contingent consideration measured at fair value
rubrics_metrics.description: The purchase price (numerator) must include the fair value of contingent consideration that is required to be recognized at fair value by the registrant at the acquisition date under the applicable GAAP (US GAAP or IFRS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When contingent consideration is in the scope of Topic 815 (derivatives) or otherwise required to be measured at fair value, include that fair value in the cost of the asset and in the numerator of the investment test. See Question 3.4.40 and related discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of contingent consideration for equity method investments
rubrics_metrics.description: When acquiring an equity method investment, the registrant recognizes only the cash purchase price as its initial investment; contingent consideration is not accounted for at the acquisition date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of the investment test, contingent consideration is included in the numerator only if the likelihood of payment is more than remote. If likelihood is remote, do not include it (Example 3.4.40 illustrates remote vs. more-than-remote outcomes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingent consideration in asset acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: For asset acquisitions, contingent consideration is generally recognized when it is probable and estimable; exceptions apply when GAAP requires fair-value measurement under other Topics (e.g., Topic 815).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contingent consideration measured at fair value under other GAAP is included in the cost of the asset and in the numerator of the investment test. Otherwise, include contingent consideration in the numerator when probable and estimable. See Question 3.4.50 and related discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other payments negotiated in contemplation of the acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments made under agreements executed in connection with the business acquisition that would not have been made had there been no acquisition are included in the numerator of the investment test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such payments may include amounts under royalty agreements, noncompete agreements, long-term lease agreements, and agreements to acquire assets owned separately by shareholders. (Question 3.4.60 and Example 3.4.50 — noncompete payments included).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of transaction costs for business combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: For business acquisitions accounted for as business combinations under US GAAP, transaction costs are not included in the purchase price (numerator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under Topic 805, transaction costs are expensed in the periods incurred and are not included in the fair value of consideration transferred to the selling shareholders. [Regs Comm 04/2008; Question 3.4.70]

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of transaction costs for equity method investments
rubrics_metrics.description: Transaction costs are included in the numerator when performing the investment test for equity method investments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transaction costs are included in the initial cost of the equity method investment under Subtopic 323-10 and therefore included in the numerator. [FRM 2015.5 note, 323-10-30-2; Question 3.4.80]

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of transaction costs for asset acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Transaction costs are included in the numerator when the acquisition is accounted for as an asset acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transaction costs are included in the initial cost of the asset under Subtopic 805-50 and thus included in the investment test numerator. See section 3.2 of KPMG Handbook, Asset acquisitions and Question 3.4.90.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment test numerator for step (staged) acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: For acquisitions achieved in stages, the investment test uses the purchase price (fair value of consideration transferred) of the incremental interests acquired (i.e., the incremental purchase price is the numerator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate step acquisitions that are part of a single plan to be completed within a 12-month period (numerators aggregated for those steps). Remeasurement gains/losses on previously held equity interests recognized under Topic 805 are not included in the numerator. (Question 3.4.100 and examples 3.4.60–3.4.80)

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment test formula (basic) — numerator / denominator
rubrics_metrics.description: Investment test = (purchase price of ownership interest acquired) ÷ (registrant’s AWMV).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply this formula using the appropriate purchase price (including items required by prior guidance) and the AWMV as defined in Rule 1-02(w). Examples throughout (e.g., Example 3.4.40, 3.4.60) illustrate calculations and thresholds for significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and calculation of AWMV (denominator)
rubrics_metrics.description: AWMV is calculated by multiplying the aggregate number of publicly traded voting and non-voting common equity shares outstanding by the price at which the common equity was last sold (or average of bid and ask) in the principal market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AWMV used in the denominator is the five-day average of AWMV for the prior five trading days of the registrant’s most recently completed month ending before the earlier of the announcement date or the agreement date. 'Month' is calendar month. Only publicly traded common shares are included regardless of exchangeability or conversion rights. AWMV includes value of equity held by affiliates and differs from Rule 12b-2 calculations. (Question 3.4.110)

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement date and agreement date: definitions and application
rubrics_metrics.description: Announcement date generally represents the date the event or transaction is first publicly announced; agreement date generally represents the date when a contract or agreement is executed and becomes legally binding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 1-02(w) does not define these terms specifically for AWMV; SEC staff expects consistent application across rules and consultation with legal counsel may be necessary. Examples reference 17 CFR § 230.165(f)(3) and Form 8-K Item 1.01(b) guidance. (Question 3.4.120)

rubrics_metrics.name: Recalculation of AWMV after announcement date changes
rubrics_metrics.description: AWMV is determined based on the earlier of the announcement date or the agreement date and is not re‑calculated after the announcement date even if there is a significant delay or change, absent consultation with the SEC staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A registrant may consult with the SEC staff if it believes a change to the date used to determine AWMV is warranted because of significant changes to transaction terms after the announcement date. (Question 3.4.130)

rubrics_metrics.name: Performing aggregate investment tests for multiple acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple acquisitions must be evaluated in the aggregate (related acquisitions or unrelated acquisitions otherwise individually insignificant), perform separate investment tests for each acquisition and then add them together (unless acquired businesses are under common control).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute AWMV separately for each acquisition based on its own announcement or agreement date; for acquisitions conditioned on one another the AWMV used will likely be the same. (Question 3.4.140)

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment test when combining entities under common control
rubrics_metrics.description: For combinations of entities under common control, the investment test is met when either: (a) net book value of the tested subsidiary exceeds 10% of the registrant’s consolidated total assets; or (b) the number of common shares exchanged exceeds 10% of registrant’s total common shares outstanding at initiation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules 3-05 and 11-01 clarify that the thresholds for providing financial statements and pro forma information apply when these conditions exceed 20% (instead of 10%). Perform both comparisons; the higher resulting significance is used. (Question 3.4.150 and Example 3.4.100)

rubrics_metrics.name: Denominator when registrant has no AWMV
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant does not have an AWMV (e.g., pre-IPO), use consolidated total assets as of the end of the most recent fiscal year for which financial statements are required as the denominator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine consolidated total assets consistent with the asset test. (Question 3.4.160)

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to use of AWMV (S-X rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: AWMV is not used for ongoing assessments under S-X Rule 3-09 (separate financial statements of subsidiaries not consolidated and 50% or less owned persons) and S-X Rule 4-08(g) (summarized financial information of subsidiaries not consolidated and 50% or less owned persons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For those rules, use the registrant’s consolidated total assets as the denominator when calculating the investment test. (Question 3.4.170)

rubrics_metrics.name: Income test: two components and overall rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The income test includes a pretax income component and a revenue component; the lower percentage of the two components is the income-test significance level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the income test to indicate a business acquisition is significant, both components must exceed 20%. If the revenue component does not apply (e.g., lack of material recurring revenue), only the pretax income component applies (with modifications in certain circumstances). (Overview and Question 3.5.10, decision-tree guidance)

rubrics_metrics.name: Pretax income component formula and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Pretax income component = (Registrant’s share of the acquired business’s pretax income) ÷ (Registrant’s consolidated pretax income), using absolute values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerator includes direct and indirect ownership interests, is income from continuing operations before income taxes after eliminating intercompany transactions and attributing NCI. Pretax income cannot be adjusted for nonrecurring or special charges or credits. Use a modified denominator (five-year average) if the revenue component does not apply and the registrant’s most recent fiscal year pretax income is at least 10% lower than the five-year average. (Question 3.5.20 and related guidance)

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculating registrant’s share of pretax income when NCI exists
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant acquires 100% of a business that itself reports NCI, use pretax income attributable to controlling interest. If acquiring less than 100%, multiply the acquired business’s pretax income (or controlling-interest pretax income if it has its own NCI) by the percentage acquired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same approach applies when a registrant’s consolidated but less-than-wholly-owned subsidiary acquires 100% of a business. This guidance aligns with the asset test and the revenue component. (Question 3.5.30 and Example 3.5.10)
